Mount Wutai, Embracing the Wonders of Nature
programs.desc: Mount Wutai, in the northeastern part of Shanxi Province, is one of the Four Great Buddhist Mountains of China. It is a magnet for tourists, who are drawn here not only by its profound Buddhist cultural heritage, but also by the spectacular natural scenery. Mount Wutai is noted for its unique topography, marked by five flattened peaks. Hence the name "Wutai," or "Five Terraces." The five, each with its own characteristics and distinct shape, are Wanghai East Peak, Guayue West Peak, Jinxiu South Peak, Yedou North Peak, and Cuiyan Central Peak. Soaring into the clouds, together they resemble a magnificent work crafted by nature.

Harbin: Moscow of the Orient
programs.desc: This episode shows Harbin's century-old Central Street brimming with exotic charm, unique Chinese Baroque architecture and authentic exquisite Russian food.We enjoy drinks at the annual Harbin Beer Festival and taste the exclusive Northern-style Manchu-Han Feast. At Volga Manor, we appreciate classic Russian architecture and folk customs from all over the world. It vividly presents Harbin, a city combining Northeast Chinese features and profound Russian cultural heritage.

Tasting the Lifestyle of Chongqing
programs.desc: This episode uncovers Chongqing's lifestyle, where hot pot is more than food but a city symbol intertwined with climate and history. Tracing its roots at a hot pot museum and experiencing mountain restaurants, we see its evolution from dockworkers' fare to a trendy lifestyle. Exploring graffiti streets, old teahouses and Hongyadong, we find Chongqing balances vibrancy and leisure amid modern development.

programs.title: Indigo Dreams: A Hue of Dali Tie-dye
programs.desc: Dali Tie-dye is the unique textile art of the Bai people, renowned for its exquisite hand-tying and traditional indigo dyeing techniques that create brilliant, one-of-a-kind patterns. Explore the cultural heritage and enduring beauty of this ancient craft from Yunnan.

programs.title: Eat Like the Locals Ep.2
programs.desc: The documentary series follows a team of foodies across 22 cities in 11 Chinese provinces, exploring local cuisines and customs against a backdrop of rich social diversity.

programs.title: Between Heaven and Earth : Traveling Through Grasslands Ep.5
programs.desc: The first season of the "Wandering the World" series follows a traveler across six of China's greatest grasslands, revealing the natural beauty of their epic landscapes and the distinctive lives of the people who inhabit them.

programs.title: Now, Guizhou Ep.2
programs.desc: This is Guizhou's first documentary combining landscape and culture that centers on the province's natural ecosystems and karst landforms. Built around eight themes - mountains, water, dwellings, caves, bridges, accessories, songs, and the future - it uses 24 personal stories to showcase Guizhou's natural and cultural beauty. The documentary traces the area's history and culture through its cultural relics.

programs.title: Aerial China IV: Xizang
programs.desc: A world-renowned wonderland of snow-capped peaks and river sources, Xizang is also a land of tradition, deep culture and spirituality. However, Xizang also has plenty to boast of in terms of its natural history and wonders. So join us as we fly over the roof of the world to survey the plateau where Tibetan antelopes, wild yaks and people live in harmony!

programs.title: Harmony Keepers: Guardians of golden snub-nosed monkeys
programs.desc: This documentary series pays tribute to the guardians of China's rare wildlife and their habitats. Through the lens of ecological protection and preservation, the series features four iconic protected species in China: the Tibetan antelope, milu deer, black-necked cranes, and golden snub-nosed monkeys.
